activity.notes: Abd Allah al-Mahdi Billah founded the Fatimid Caliphate in 909 and ruled as its first Isma'ili imam-caliph until 934. The user offered either al-Mahdi or al-Mu'izz as the civilization's representative; ATLAS selects al-Mahdi because the request permits either and his reign is the founding reign of the Fatimid state. This does not imply that al-Mu'izz, who later conquered Egypt and presided over a major expansion, lacks independent registration value.

sources.title: UBEYDULLAH el-MEHDÎ — TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
sources.citation_text: The TDV Encyclopedia of Islam identifies al-Mahdi as the founder of the Fatimids and the first openly recognized Isma'ili imam, ruling from 909 to 934.

sources.title: A History of Shiʿi Islam
sources.citation_text: Farhad Daftary's history identifies the establishment of the Fatimid caliphate in 909 under Abd Allah al-Mahdi and gives his reign as 909–934.
